Single crystals of CoP3 were grown from a stoichiometric melt under a pressure of 3.5 GPa using a wedge-type, cubic-anvil, high-pressure apparatus.
The as-grown boules of CoP3 were typically 3.4 mm in diameter and split easily along the radial direction to generate specimens around 1 mm in diameter and 0.3 mm in length.
Powder X-ray diffraction measurements confirmed that the as-grown boules were a single phase of CoP3, with no impurity phases observed.
The lattice constant of the grown CoP3 crystals, determined by powder X-ray diffraction, was 7.7067 Å, close to the literature value.
SEM-EDS measurements found a Co:P ratio of 0.97:3.00 in the as-grown CoP3 crystals, consistent with the stoichiometric composition.
Back-reflection Laue X-ray measurements showed 2mm symmetry, indicating that the grown specimens were single crystals.
The results suggest that CoP3 is a congruent melting compound under high pressure, in contrast to other skutterudites that are known to be incongruent melting compounds at ambient pressure.
Growing large single crystals of skutterudites is important for studying their fundamental properties, such as the origin of their low thermal conductivity and superior thermoelectric performance.
Limitations of the flux method for growing skutterudite single crystals include the ability to crystallize only a few compounds and the small size of the grown crystals.
Potential solutions suggested for increasing the size of the CoP3 single crystals include using a slower cooling rate and applying a more homogeneous pressure.
The high-pressure, cubic-anvil technique used in this study was previously applied to enhance the growth of black phosphorus single crystals.
The as-grown CoP3 boules were characterized by powder X-ray diffraction, SEM-EDS, and back-reflection Laue X-ray measurements.
